title: The UN commission's report ties the conflict to the failure to unify Korea
summary: The UN Korea commission says the conflict followed the failure to create one independent Korea.
body: The UN commission report, as Fordham prints it, says that had a unified and independent Korea come into existence, the present conflict could never have arisen, and it calls the Korean people one in race, language, and culture. The report is the commission's political reading. It is not Gromyko's sentence about who fired first. The wording on the page includes: "supervised elections been allowed to take place in the whole of Korea, and had a unified and independent Korea thereby come into existence, the present conflict could never have arisen. C. Prospects of unification. The Korean people, one in race, language and culture, fervently desire to live in a unified and independent Korea. Unification can be the only aim". The evidence label is the truth-gate ceiling for this host. The host is not on the gate's primary-text or official list, so the label is weak. The quotation is still the page's wording.
